$comment: The six things a country can lead on. A lens is not a tag applied to everything — every country in the set has all twenty-seven categories written up, so filtering on those would light the whole map and tell a traveller nothing. A lens is what a country declares in its own `calls`, which is editorial and deliberately short: Uganda calls wildlife and culture, and does not call coast, even though it has lakes. `categories` is the other direction — which of the twenty-seven write-ups belong to this lens, so opening a country under a lens leads with the right places.

wildlife.title: Wildlife
wildlife.line: Where the animals are the reason you came.

culture.title: Culture
culture.line: Kingdoms, languages, festivals and the people who keep them.

coast.title: Coast
coast.line: Atlantic, Indian Ocean, Mediterranean, and the lakes big enough to have surf.

heritage.title: Heritage
heritage.line: What was built here, and what is still standing.

mountains.title: Mountains
mountains.line: The Atlas, the Rwenzori, Kilimanjaro, the Simien, Fako.

food.title: Food
food.line: What a country actually eats, not what it serves tourists.

$comment_words: What somebody might actually type. The intent parser matches against these and against nothing else — no stemming, no fuzzy matching, no model. A word that is not in one of these lists simply does not select a lens, which is the correct behaviour: guessing at what somebody meant and being wrong is worse than asking. Every entry here is a word for the thing the lens already covers; none of them extends what a lens means.
